clues.title: Road line: Greece double white lines
text: In Greece you will commonly see slightly faded, solid white double middle lines. This can be used to distinguish it from most other Mediterranean countries.

clues.title: Pole: Greek lamps

clues.title: Greece
text: **Horizontal Zebra stripe**: Austria, Belgium, Greece, Poland, Serbia. > **Detailed guy with no hat**: Greece. Note that Greece's icon has hair that may almost look like a hat but it's just hair. Kinda looks like the Dame Tu Cosita guy

clues.title: Bollard: Bollard
text: Greek bollards are wedge-shaped with almost square reflectors, being red on the front and white on the back.
Andorra bollards are similar but landscape/vegetation will be way different most of the time.

clues.title: Language: Greek language
text: The Greek language features a unique alphabet not used in any other language. It shares similarities with both the latin and cyrillic alphabet, however the lower case letters generally have softer shapes than the cyrillic letters.

clues.title: Landscape: Flat Valleys
text: The largest flat agricultural valleys in Greece are found close to Thessaloniki and Larissa, but smaller flat valleys, where the mountains generally appear closer, can be found in several other areas in the north and centre of the country.

clues.title: Landscape: Mount Pangaion
text: Mount Pangaion can be recognised from its shape, being more of a solitary mountain rather than a wide mountain range, combined with the fact that it is located to the south of a flat agricultural valley.

clues.title: Architecture: Mediterranean Architecture
text: **Greek architecture shares a lot of features with other Mediterranean countries:**
A lot of white and pastel-coloured stone houses with orange tiled roofs.
White houses are very common when compared to most other Mediterranean countries.
Urban residential buildings will generally be multi-floored, light-coloured and typically have connected balconies along one or multiple walls.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Cyclade Islands - White Walls & Blue Doors
text: **One of the most well-known types of Greek architecture:**
Houses with completely white walls, blue doors and shutters, is mainly found on the small central Cyclade islands.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Greece
text: Greek area codes will always begin with a 2, followed by 1-3 digits determining the area.
NOTE: If the third digit is 1, you will be in the largest city of the region, and if the third digit is 9, you will be in the area surrounding that city.
